newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARIAN SHARES SEEN CONTINUING RECORD BULL RUN.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARIAN SHARES SEEN CONTINUING RECORD BULL RUN.

text.p: Hungary's BUX share index was seen rising to the seventh successive record high on Monday after getting new fuel from Friday's record on Wall Street and positive developments in the Hungarian economy, traders said.
"I expect a moderate rise... perhaps by between 30 to 50 points," said Tamas Moro of Procent Hungaria.
The BUX index put on 60.76 points on Friday, to finish at 6,319.01, but following more than one week of sharp rises the run was likely to lose some steam, traders said.
However, almost all domestic and international news were encouraging for investors looking at Hungarian shares, traders said.
"Friday's good U.S. bourse figures will certainly make (Hungarian) shares rise," Moro said.
Another trader added that the dollar's fall against the forint was unlikely to affect the market.
"The dollar eased a little, but it is still at relatively high levels," Gyorgy Czipo of ING Barings said.

Traders said the current account figures published on Friday, showing that Hungary posted current account and trade surpluses in March after several months of deficits, gave good signals about the state of the economy.
The central bank's 0.5 percentage point cuts in four of its five repo rates on Friday reflected the fall of inflation and also indicated improvement in the economy, they added.
Czipo said the Hungarian market usually reacted slowly to developments in the macroeconomy, but he added that foreign investors' buying appetite did not subside even after last week's bull run.
"There are still funds waiting to invest," he said, adding that the situation of the Czech economy was still uncertain and this prompted investors to allocate more funds to Hungary.
